title: What Actually Happens to a Body in Space?
hook: Part 1: A boiling kettle and an astronaut share the exact same nightmare.
script: Part 1: A boiling kettle and an astronaut share the exact same nightmare. What actually happens if an airlock flings you into space? You do not freeze solid or explode like movies always promised. Instead, exposure to vacuum instantly removes all surrounding pressure. This triggers ebullism, making water in your body boil at room temperature. In a 1966 NASA test, a subject felt saliva bubbling on his tongue. You keep just 15 seconds of consciousness before oxygen leaves your blood. Could you stay calm for those 15 seconds? Follow for part 2.
